text:
Alexandre Carrier plays 20 minutes a night on Montreal's right side, blocks shots (38 so far) and doesn't score much, which is what he's always done. He has seven points in 20 games and Dose.ca recently described a bad three-game stretch.

The numbers back up the concern more than the points do. Montreal takes 43% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) with Carrier on the ice, almost 11 points worse than without him, and 45% of the shot attempts. The Canadiens have scored 8.0 more goals than expected during his shifts, which has kept the results looking fine. That's the clearest example on this roster of the team's results running ahead of its play.

Evolving-Hockey had him as a solid, middle-of-the-pack defenseman last season, 88th of 215, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking doesn't find a standout weakness. Our model compares him to Troy Stecher and Nick Perbix, defensemen whose teams tend to spend time in their own end with them out there. Our talent range has him around 29 points. If the luck turns, he's one of the Habs who will feel it.
